insights: The planar Ceva product BD/DC·CE/EA·AF/FB = 1 is the single-triangle instance of a 1-cocycle condition on a simplex's edge ratios r(i,j)=w_j/w_i.
Higher-dimensional Ceva (open Q4): cevians of an n-simplex concur iff the classical Ceva equation holds on EVERY triangular 2-face; the triangle conditions generate the whole concurrency relation.
Concurrency = solvability: a positive edge-ratio assignment comes from a common point iff it is a coboundary r(i,j)=w_j/w_i, i.e. iff it satisfies the cocycle law r(i,j)·r(j,k)=r(i,k).
The concurrency point is reconstructed CONSTRUCTIVELY: its barycentric coordinates are w_i = r(b,i) for any base vertex b.
The cube relation r(i,i)^3=1 with positivity forces r(i,i)=1 (factor x^2+x+1>0) — the only nonlinear step, and what makes the triangle conditions sufficient for the cocycle.
Telescoping ∏ f(t+1)/f(t)=f(m)/f(0) gives Ceva around ANY closed walk (e.g. a tetrahedron's 4-vertex loop), unifying all ratio-product identities.

Child cevas-theorem-oq-02-oq-04-oq-01 (PR-pending) builds the Menelaus DUAL of this Ceva cocycle: signed ratio m(i,j)=-a_i/a_j, twisted cocycle m(i,j)·m(j,k)=-m(i,k), 2-face product -1, reconstruction a_i=1/m(b,i), and duality m(i,j)=-r(j,i) — resolves the listed Menelaus higher-dim next-step.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has no abstract 1-cocycle/coboundary theory on a complete graph specialized to barycentric edge ratios; built self-contained (~290 lines).
Full geometric (Riemannian) formalization of simplex cevians as hypersurfaces remains open — this entry is the algebraic core, not the embedded-geometry statement.
nextSteps: Connect edge-ratio cocycle to an actual affine/barycentric point in Mathlib (Affine.Simplex, barycentric coords) for the embedded-geometry version.
Menelaus analogue in higher dimensions: signed edge ratios with product −1 around faces (transversal hyperplane criterion).
